title: Uniform ideal-power cohomology image bound for algebraic spaces
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a proper morphism of algebraic spaces [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed. Work with module sheaves on the small etale ringed site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $F$ be coherent: it is quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and on every Noetherian affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ is associated to a finitely generated $R$-module. Put $J=I\mathcal O_X$ and let $J^nF$ be the submodule of $F$ locally generated by products of $n$ local sections of $J$ and a section of $F$, with $J^0F=F$. For $q\geq0$ put $M_n=H^q(X,J^nF)$, where $H^q$ is the right derived global sections of the underlying additive sheaf [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with its $A$-action induced by $f^\sharp$. For $r\geq n$ let $u_{r,n}:M_r\to M_n$ be induced by inclusion. There is an integer $c\geq0$ such that for all integers $n\geq0$ and $m\geq c$,
$$\operatorname{Im}(u_{n+m,n})\subseteq I^{m-c}M_n.$$
Here $I^tM_n$ is the submodule consisting of finite sums of $ax$ with $a\in I^t$ and $x\in M_n$. No localness or completeness of $A$, flatness of $F$, or schematicity of $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08AX, lemma-cohomology-powers-ideal-application, part (2), in the preceding situation-formal-functions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-cohomology-powers-rees-finite] to the given $A,I,f,F,q$. It supplies the finite $B=\mathcal R_A(I)$-module $\bigoplus_r M_r$, the maps $L(k,r,a)$ induced by the specified sheaf multiplication maps, the convolution formula, and the identity $L(0,r,a)(x)=ax$. All hypotheses are exactly those of the item; no flatness or schematicity is used.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-rees-module-single-degree-generation] to these $A$-modules and maps, using the finite module structure, convolution formula and degree-zero identity just obtained. Choose its $c_0$ and put $c=c_0$. Thus whenever $d\geq c$ and $k\geq0$, $M_{d+k}$ is the $A$-span of $L(k,d,a)(x)$ with $a\in I^k$ and $x\in M_d$.

For $d\geq n$, the two sheaf maps $J^dF\to J^nF$ obtained by first multiplying by $a\in I^k$ and including from degree $d+k$, or first including from degree $d$ and multiplying in degree zero, are equal. Indeed, after their injective inclusions into $F$, both send every local section $s$ to $f^\sharp(a)s$, by the formula in [lem-sfb-space-cohomology-powers-rees-finite]. Functoriality of cohomology [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and the degree-zero identity therefore give $u_{d+k,n}L(k,d,a)(x)=a\,u_{d,n}(x)$. The inclusion maps on cohomology are additive and $A$-linear: the same equality of section maps with arbitrary degree-zero scalars proves commutation with every $a\in A$.

Fix $n\geq0$ and $m\geq c$. Set $d=\max(n,c)$ and $k=n+m-d$. Then $d\geq n,c$, $k\geq0$, $d+k=n+m$ and $k\geq m-c$. By step 2 every $y\in M_{n+m}$ is a finite $A$-linear combination of $L(k,d,a)(x)$. Step 3 takes each such term to $a\,u_{d,n}(x)\in I^kM_n$. Additivity and $A$-linearity handle the finite combination. Finally, $I^k=I^{m-c}I^{k-(m-c)}\subseteq I^{m-c}$, so $u_{n+m,n}(y)\in I^{m-c}M_n$, as required.

lean.statement: theorem space_ideal_power_cohomology_image_bound (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (X : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of A))) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of A))))) (hf : MapIsProper f) (F : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsFinitePresentation) (q : ℕ) : ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ n m : ℕ, c ≤ m → LinearMap.range ((baseScalarCohomology X f q).map (baseIdealPowerSmallInclusion X I F (n + m) n (Nat.le_add_right n m))).hom ≤ I ^ (m - c) • (⊤ : Submodule A ((baseScalarCohomology X f q).obj (baseIdealPowerSmallModule X I F n)))
lean.note: Ideal powers are kernels of the existing canonical sheaf quotient projections, transported by the existing small-ringed-model equivalence; the inclusions are kernel maps of the normalized quotient transitions. Cohomology specializes the existing affineScalarSections right derived functor in all module sheaves, with its structural A-action; Stacks 03FD gives underlying-additive cohomology naturally. On the locally Noetherian space supplied by properness over A, Mathlib IsFinitePresentation is precisely coherence (Stacks 07UB). The three added statement dependencies are already landed definitions, permitted by brief-stage2 section 5; no node statement or proof is changed.
